segments.t: Troubled by his hallucinations of his late mother-in-law, Chef Barinov visits his doctor friend, who examines his test results and delivers a grim warning about his heart.
Ладно тебе, я даже болезней таких не знаю.
У тебя очень слабый организм.
И сердце слабое.
Инсульт даром не проходит.
И галлюцинации просто так не появляются.
И сколько мне осталось?
Может пять лет, а может и год.
Тебе надо бросить работу.
Бросить совсем?
Готовь спокойно у себя дома на кухне.
Но никаких стрессов на работе.
Я тебя услышал.
Now let's go back through their conversation line by line and unpack the Russian phrasing.
Ладно тебе, я даже болезней таких не знаю.
'Come on, I do not even know such illnesses.' Chef Barinov anchors the line on 'all right', while 'know' completes the thought.
У тебя очень слабый организм.
'Your body is very weak.' The grammar packs 'at' and 'body' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
И сердце слабое.
'And your heart is weak.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'and' and finishing on 'weak'.
Инсульт даром не проходит.
'A stroke does not pass without consequences.' the doctor brings out the contrast between 'stroke' and 'gift' in a few short words.
И галлюцинации просто так не появляются.
'And hallucinations do not appear out of nowhere.' the doctor anchors the line on 'and', while 'to appear' completes the thought.
И сколько мне осталось?
'And how much time do I have left?' The grammar packs 'and' and 'remained' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange. the doctor answers right away.
Может пять лет, а может и год.
'Maybe five years, or maybe a year.' the doctor anchors the line on 'maybe', while 'year' completes the thought.
Тебе надо бросить работу.
'You need to quit your job.' The grammar packs 'to you' and 'work' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
Бросить совсем?
'Quit completely?' Notice how Russian expresses 'to abandon' and 'at all' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. the doctor answers right away.
Готовь спокойно у себя дома на кухне.
'Cook calmly at home in your own kitchen.' In Russian, the idea of 'prepare' flows naturally into 'kitchen' without extra filler words.
Но никаких стрессов на работе.
'But no stresses at work.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'but' and finishing on 'work'.
Я тебя услышал.
'I heard you.' The grammar packs 'I' and 'heard' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange. Alright, let's hear the entire conversation one more time from start to finish.

Готовь спокойно у себя дома на кухне.

Ordered to give up professional cooking for the sake of his life, Barinov protests that his lifelong dream is finally within reach. See you in the next scene.
Береги своё сердце, Витя.
